lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Write a four-sentence sculpture response covering views, materials, meaning+evidence and a respectful question.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: Includes at least two views, material note, evidenced meaning and a question that does not assume secret knowledge.

WATCH FOR
Touching museum work or guessing sacred meanings. Look with eyes; ask educators about protocols.

INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Respond to a sculpture (photo or visit) with a full write-up and a labelled sketch of front and side views.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example: 'From the front the figure leans forward; from the side the base is triangular for balance. The rough texture suggests wind. I think it is about facing weather because of the lean and rough surface.'

TRY FIRST
Write a four-sentence sculpture response covering views, materials, meaning+evidence and a respectful question.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: Includes at least two views, material note, evidenced meaning and a question that does not assume secret knowledge.
teach_steps.explain:
Responding to a sculpture includes describing form from more than one view, noting mass/space, materials and possible meaning with evidence. If you cannot walk around a real work, use multiple photos. Stay respectful of cultural works: some First Nations carved or woven objects carry restricted knowledge—use only approved classroom information and do not invent sacred meanings.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the elements, techniques or performance choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For movement or instruments, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby and stop if anything feels unsafe. You may always describe a choice instead of performing it. One deliberate artistic choice with a named effect is more useful than a longer praise sentence.
teach_steps.notice: Touching museum work or guessing sacred meanings. Look with eyes; ask educators about protocols. Name the element or technique and its effect, not just decoration.
